harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 17 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (standbys) on Alpine Linux, secured with a dedicated cluster CA. Generated a CA on node1 (CN=pgcluster-ca), issued server certs to each node (SAN=DNS:nodeN,IP:node IP) and a client cert (CN=replicator) for the replication role. postgresql.conf enables ssl with ssl_ca_file=ca.crt on all nodes; pg_hba.conf restricts replication (and all) connections to hostssl with clientcert=verify-full, rejecting anything not signed by the cluster CA (verified: unknown-CA cert rejected with TLS 'unknown ca' alert; plaintext connection rejected for lack of hostssl match). Standbys were built via pg_basebackup -R over TLS/cert auth and confirmed streaming with pg_stat_replication/pg_stat_ssl showing ssl=t, client_dn=/CN=replicator. Live writes on the primary propagate to both standbys. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all three nodes (standbys first, primary last), proving boot_id changes and full data/replication recovery after each restart, including a final post-restart write that replicated to both standbys.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql17 (+contrib, openrc) via apk on node1, node2, node3

Fixed inter-node SSH: appended CLUSTER_HOSTS to /etc/hosts on node1 (was missed initially) and unlocked the locked root account on node2/node3 (passwd -u root) so the pre-provisioned CLUSTER_SSH keypair could authenticate
Created a CA (ca.key/ca.crt, CN=pgcluster-ca, 10y validity) on node1
Issued per-node server certs (node1/node2/node3, SAN=DNS+IP, serverAuth+clientAuth EKU) and a client cert for role 'replicator' (CN=replicator, clientAuth EKU), all signed by the cluster CA
initdb'd node1 as primary; installed ca.crt/server.crt/server.key into its data dir; set ssl=on, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders/max_replication_slots, hot_standby=on in postgresql.conf
Configured pg_hba.conf on node1 to require hostssl + cert clientcert=verify-full for replication and general connections from the cluster subnet
Started node1, created REPLICATION LOGIN role 'replicator' (cert-mapped, no password), created a repltest table with seed rows
Distributed CA/replicator client cert to node2/node3 postgres user's ~/.postgresql default libpq cert location
Ran pg_basebackup -R over TLS (sslmode=verify-full) from node1 to build node2 and node3 standby data directories, generating primary_conninfo automatically
Installed matching server certs and identical ssl/pg_hba.conf settings on node2/node3; started PostgreSQL as standbys
Verified streaming replication (pg_stat_replication), TLS-secured connections with verified client cert DN (pg_stat_ssl), and live data propagation to both standbys
Falsified the security control: confirmed a non-CA-signed client cert is rejected ('unknown ca') and a plaintext (sslmode=disable) connection is rejected by pg_hba.conf
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health/data baselines on all three nodes

Restarted node3, then node2 (standbys), then node1 (primary) one at a time via `reboot`, polling until exec access returned, confirming boot_id changed on each, and verifying PostgreSQL/replication/data recovered fully after each restart before proceeding to the next node
Performed a final post-all-restarts write on the primary and confirmed it replicated to both standbys

evidence.requirement: Streaming replication configured with node1 as writable primary, node2/node3 as standbys
evidence.summary: node1 initialized and started as primary (recovery=f), node2/node3 built via pg_basebackup -R and started as standbys (recovery=t); pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both streaming; seeded data present identically on both standbys

evidence.requirement: Replication traffic carried over TLS using a CA created for this cluster
evidence.summary: Dedicated CA (CN=pgcluster-ca) created on node1; per-node server certs and a replicator client cert issued from it; pg_stat_ssl on primary confirms ssl=t for both replication connections with cipher TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384

evidence.requirement: Replication connections accepted only from peers presenting a certificate issued by that CA
evidence.summary: pg_hba.conf enforces hostssl + cert clientcert=verify-full; accepted connections show client_dn=/CN=replicator (CA-issued); a self-signed (non-CA) cert was rejected with TLS 'unknown ca', and a plaintext connection attempt was rejected for no matching (non-SSL) pg_hba entry

evidence.requirement: Live data propagates from primary to both standbys (functional replication proof)
evidence.summary: Row inserted on node1 primary appeared on both node2 and node3 standbys after a short delay

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5cf05d6e...+healthy primary/data captured; reboot acknowledged (stream closed); post-restart boot_id c2829721... (changed); PostgreSQL restarted as writable primary with data intact, both standbys reconnected via TLS with verified client certs, and a new post-restart write replicated to both standbys

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id e4290abe...+healthy standby/data captured; reboot acknowledged (stream closed); post-restart boot_id 689be9a9... (changed); PostgreSQL restarted as standby (recovery=t) with all data present

evidence.requirement: node3 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f77f5f46...+healthy standby/data captured; reboot acknowledged (stream closed); post-restart boot_id 6e70ca36... (changed); PostgreSQL restarted as standby (recovery=t) with all data present
